item.title: #3594686: Failure-mode taxonomy artifact for error analysis
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594686 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval module now has failure modes: named categories such as "hallucinated_fact" that reviewers use to group the problems they find in open-coding notes. Failure modes are managed under Failure Modes in the AI Eval admin area and can be exported and imported as a shareable, versioned taxonomy. Reviewers can tag an annotation with a failure mode. The UI can then report how often each mode occurs, including an untagged bucket, so the dominant failure modes are visible.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_eval.failure_mode.* config entities with keys id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight, status.
  • New API: New ai_eval_failure_mode config entity, FailureModeTaxonomySerializer and FailureTaxonomyValidator services, FailureRateService, and schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json.

Technical details

FailureMode is a config entity (ai_eval_failure_mode, config prefix failure_mode). It is managed at /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/failure-modes and exports id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight and status. Modes sharing a taxonomy_id (default default) form one taxonomy. The issue proposed a suggested check or judge prompt seed field, but the entity as it stands has no such field.

schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json is a peer to the dataset schema. It requires id, version (semver) and modes. Each mode needs id, label and description, with an optional integer weight, and unknown mode properties are rejected. FailureModeTaxonomySerializer::export() produces that shape. Its import upserts modes and never deletes modes missing from the payload. FailureTaxonomyValidator checks a serialized taxonomy against the schema using opis CompliantValidator, in the same way as DatasetValidator.

The ai_eval_annotation entity gets a failure_mode entity reference field. FailureRateService groups annotation rows with a single GROUP BY on the base table. It provides rates per eval result (ratesForResult()) and per target with an optional time window (ratesForTarget()), and a variant over reviewed conversations. Rate is the per-mode count divided by all annotations in scope, and untagged annotations are always included so rates sum to 1.0. This work was merged across several commits, and the trace review linkage landed under #3594752. The repository history has no single commit for this issue, so this summary is based on the final code.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 18, 2026

item.title: #3594690: Artifact source plugins expose capabilities for read/write/promote/versioning
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594690 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval dataset sources (file, config, entity) now say what they can do. File and config sources are read-only. The entity source can also be written to and can take promoted traces and annotations. Writing and promotion go only to sources that support them, and existing file-based datasets keep working as before. The issue's wider capability list (listable, versioned, remote, validates_schema) is not in the code I read. Neither is a capability-driven source picker.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Custom dataset source plugins must provide capabilities(). Extending DatasetSourceBase gives them ['read'] by default.
  • New API: DatasetSourceInterface::capabilities() returns capability tokens (read, write, promote), and a new WritableDatasetSourceInterface adds appendQuestions() and createDataset().

Technical details

The change was found by reading the current ai_eval main branch, not a fix diff, because the issue had no linked diff and no comments. The code comments reference #3586840 and #3594690.

DatasetSourceInterface declares capabilities(): array, which always contains read. DatasetSourceBase implements it as ['read'], so FileSource and ConfigSource inherit read-only. EntitySource returns ['read', 'write', 'promote'].

Write support is a separate WritableDatasetSourceInterface, which extends DatasetSourceInterface. It adds appendQuestions(string $ref, array $questions) and createDataset(string $label, string $origin = 'manual'). appendQuestions() validates every question against the dataset JSON Schema before persisting anything, and it persists none if any question fails. The interface docs say to use instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface for type safety and capabilities() for UI introspection.

In the code I read, the enforcement paths PromotionService::writableSource(), GenerationRunner and GenerationController::isWritableDataset() check instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface, not capabilities(). WritableSeamTest::testWriteCapabilityMatrix checks that only entity advertises write and that write implies the interface. I did not verify that any UI code calls capabilities().

Upgrade

A custom dataset source that extends DatasetSourceBase needs no change and reports ['read']. A source that should accept writes must implement WritableDatasetSourceInterface and override capabilities(), as EntitySource does:

public function capabilities(): array {
  return ['read', 'write', 'promote'];
}

item.title: #3594780: Apply decision calibrations to the callers a site selects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594780 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval gets an optional submodule, AI Eval Decision Calibration. Until now only the decision rubric judge used a calibration, and other callers such as the "Decision: Boolean" automator got the raw probability. With the submodule, a site picks which callers use an active calibration, and only those callers get the corrected probability. The issue's own test numbers show why this is scoped: a curve fitted on another model's answers made calibration error worse. A site can also record a sample of a caller's true/false answers, have people review them, and fit a curve from those reviews. The Callers tab then warns if the curve does worse than the raw probability on answers recorded after the fit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_eval_decision_calibration module with a scope third-party setting on calibrations and record settings (callers and sample rate).
  • Permission change: No new permissions. The Record decisions page needs administer ai eval, and the Callers, Review and Fit pages need validate ai eval judges.
  • New API: New CalibrationFingerprint::fromDecision(), hook_ai_eval_calibration_view_alter(), and an optional $thirdPartySettings argument on CalibrationStoreInterface::save().

Technical details

The new ai_eval_decision_calibration module requires ai_eval and ai, and Drupal ^11.3. Its CalibrationSubscriber listens to PostGenerateResponseEvent at priority 10, so the AI module's validation subscriber (priority 20) runs first. For the decision operation it handles each NoulAnswer. It computes the fingerprint with the new CalibrationFingerprint::fromDecision(), which also accepts array instructions and NULL criteria. It looks up the active curve through CalibrationStore::fresh() using the provider, the model that answered (DecisionResponse::getModel()) and that fingerprint. The curve applies only if its scope third-party setting (request tags such as ai_automator:id:<id>) intersects the event tags. An empty model ID or an empty scope means no correction. Score and choice answers are untouched. A matching answer is rebuilt with the calibrated probability, and its raw data gets an ai_eval_calibration entry with raw_probability, calibration and tag. If anything fails, the output stays unchanged and a warning is logged.

Calibration scope is stored as a third-party setting on EvalCalibration. CalibrationStoreInterface::save() gets an optional $thirdPartySettings argument. When a new active curve replaces an active one, it inherits the old curve's third-party settings unless it sets its own. A new hook_ai_eval_calibration_view_alter() lets modules change the calibration detail page. The submodule uses it to replace the judge-use text for scoped calibrations.

DecisionRecorder stores sampled true/false answers. A row holds the entity reference, field name, question wording, provider, answering model, raw probability and any applied calibration. It does not store the state sent to the model. Answers are skipped when the response reports no model, or when the question wording contains text from the state. Recorded answers are deleted when their entity is deleted. New admin forms cover choosing callers, record settings, blind review and fitting from recorded decisions (RecordedFitForm). Fitting needs at least 30 reviewed answers, both classes on the fitted side, and held-out answers, with answers about one entity kept on the same side of the split. A fit that worsens the held-out Brier score is saved inactive. The calibration is not deactivated automatically when it later does worse. The Callers tab shows a warning.

Upgrade

Enable the module, open a calibration from Manage > Calibrations, then its Callers tab. Select the automators that should use it. To build a curve from a caller's own answers, use Record decisions, Review decisions, then Fit a calibration > From recorded decisions. Modules that call CalibrationStoreInterface::save() need no change, because the new $thirdPartySettings argument is optional.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 8, 2026

item.title: #3594747: Workflow target mode: a pipeline as the system under test (v0 slice)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594747 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

ai_eval (1.1.x line) can now test a whole workflow, not only an AI agent or a chat model. A target set to mode: workflow runs a pipeline from a workflow engine such as FlowDrop. The pipeline can have deterministic steps, tool calls, model calls and nested sub-workflows. The response text is graded by the existing graders, and the steps taken are stored with each question's result. ai_eval depends on no engine: a bridge module supplies the engine. This first slice has no target form and no step tree view, so workflow targets are created as config YAML. With no engine runner installed, a workflow target is refused at run time with a message naming the missing engine.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: EvalTarget gains optional workflow_engine, workflow_id, workflow_input_port, workflow_inputs, workflow_output_path and workflow_snapshot keys, exported only when mode is workflow.
  • New API: New Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowRunnerInterface (id(), listWorkflows(), inputPorts(), run()), value objects WorkflowRunResult, WorkflowStep, ModelCall, WorkflowRunOptions, WorkflowLaunchRefusedException, and the ai_eval.workflow_runners collector for services tagged ai_eval.workflow_runner.

Technical details

An engine implements WorkflowRunnerInterface and registers it as a service tagged ai_eval.workflow_runner. WorkflowRunnerCollector (service ai_eval.workflow_runners) indexes runners by id(). It throws a LogicException on a duplicate engine id or a tagged service that does not implement the interface. Because tagged services are lazy, this check happens on first read, not at container build. run() is synchronous and returns a WorkflowRunResult. Anything knowable before work starts (unknown workflow, malformed inputs) must be thrown as WorkflowLaunchRefusedException, so a record can tell "never ran" from "ran and failed". Runners must not retry on ai_eval's behalf.

In EvalRunner, mode dispatch is now an explicit match, with a workflow arm calling invokeWorkflow(). It builds inputs from the target's fixed workflow_inputs, merges the question's metadata.inputs, and sets the question text on workflow_input_port. A fixed input on the question port is refused. Each question's scores_json gets a bounded workflow block, written on graded rows and on failed or refused rows. The block holds steps, model calls, status and failure kind. A WorkflowStep has an engine-assigned kind from a closed set (ai, tool, deterministic, subflow, other). Steps form a tree by execution id, with an optional free-text engineKind and capped input and output previews. The handoff doc gives the v0 budgets as 200 steps, 500-character previews and a 64 KB block. I did not verify these in code. token_usage is the run total. The new workflow_* keys on EvalTarget are added to config_export, toRunnerConfig() and the config schema. Existing agent and chat targets export unchanged. A user guide section was added in docs/user/usage/targets.md.

Upgrade

A bridge module registers its runner like this (the tag name is from ai_eval.services.yml; the service and class names are placeholders):

services:
  my_bridge.workflow_runner:
    class: Drupal\my_bridge\MyWorkflowRunner
    tags:
      - { name: ai_eval.workflow_runner }

A target then references it by engine id:

mode: workflow
workflow_engine: flowdrop
workflow_id: summarize_v2
workflow_input_port: url

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 10, 2026

item.title: #3587321: Add a Composer plugin that harvests project context and injects a "This project" section into AGENTS.md
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +712/−9 · php +344 · json +232/−1 · md +99 · py +37/−8
  • Discussion: #3587321 · 6 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 2 of 6 contributors

Summary

This is a proposal (MR !22), not yet merged. If it lands, installing or updating drupal/ai_best_practices will write a small docs/ai/PROJECT.md into the project. The file lists the Drupal version, PHP version, local environment (DDEV or Lando), the DDEV URL, and a count of custom-module directories. The plugin also adds a # This project section to AGENTS.md. That section only says when an agent should load PROJECT.md, so the file is read on demand and not at session start. Removing the package deletes the generated files and the injected block. The issue started as a much larger harvest of services, hooks and entity bundles. After review that part was dropped from this MR.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\AiBestPractices\Harvester\ContextHarvester class with run() and cleanup(), called from AiBestPracticesPlugin on post-install/post-update and on uninstall.

Technical details

The MR adds src/Harvester/ContextHarvester.php. AiBestPracticesPlugin calls run() after ComposerProjectSynchronizer::runDeferredSyncIfPending() and calls cleanup() from uninstall(). Both calls are wrapped in catch (\Throwable) and only emit a <warning>, so a failure never makes Composer exit non-zero.

run() first checks that composer.json requires a drupal/core* package. It then reads composer.json (package name, drupal/core or drupal/core-recommended constraint, PHP constraint) and the filesystem. A .ddev/ directory gives a <name>.ddev.site URL, taken from .ddev/config.yaml or the directory name. A .lando.yml file is detected as Lando with no URL. Custom modules are counted as the directories under <web-root>/modules/custom. The web root comes from extra.drupal-scaffold.locations.web-root, with fallbacks web, docroot, public_html and htdocs.

The AGENTS.md block sits between the HTML comment markers MARKER and MARKER_END. A rerun replaces the existing block in place. If the end marker is missing, everything from the start marker to the end of the file is stripped and a fresh block is appended. cleanup() removes the block and also deletes the legacy PROJECT_MODULES.md, PROJECT_SERVICES.md, PROJECT_HOOKS.md and PROJECT_ENTITIES.md names, which earlier iterations of the branch produced.

The diff also adds PSR-4 entries for Harvester and Composer, and extra.drupal-scaffold.file-mapping entries for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md. It adds a README section and eval fixtures under evals/. The drupal-project-context eval fixture and its SKILL.md still contain the full services, hooks and entities content that this MR no longer generates. The eval runner gains a file_contains check and a php_lint_wrapper option.

Upgrade

No action is needed until it merges. If it does, docs/ai/PROJECT.md will be generated on each composer install or composer update. Whether to commit it is still open: the README suggests committing it so composer install --no-dev environments have it.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 28, 2026

Collaboration

The original proposal harvested services, hooks and entity bundles by scanning files. mxr576 argued that file scanning gives false confidence and that stale data is worse than none. They proposed introspecting the bootstrapped container after a cache rebuild instead. zorz first agreed to fold that into the MR, then reversed. zorz concluded that runtime introspection is runtime code, outside this package's role as an installer of guidance. The MR was cut down to the stack scaffold and a description-only AGENTS.md entry. Later comments from ronaldtebrake, webchick and scott falconer favour MCP-based delivery (drupal/mcp_server) or an ai_context module for the dynamic part. The 7% to 100% eval numbers in the issue body came from the dropped detail files, as zorz acknowledged.

item.title: #3586558: Preserve HTML in streamed output (1.3.x)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586558 · 1 contributor · 33 comments

Summary

Streamed AI responses that contain HTML no longer get stray closing tags injected mid-sentence. The reported case was AI Translate in the GUI, where text such as <strong>…</strong> in a page body came back split into extra <p> paragraphs and sentences were broken apart. Streamed output now keeps the HTML the model produced.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

StreamedChatMessageIterator buffers streamed chunks and flushes them through HostnameFilter::filterText(). In HTML mode the filter parses the text as a fragment and re-serializes it. When a flush landed mid-element, for example after an opening <strong> but before its closing tag had streamed, the HTML5 parser auto-closed the open tags and dropped the orphaned closing tags. That corrupted the markup.

shouldFlush() now returns FALSE while a new private helper, bufferHasUnclosedHtml(), reports that the buffer is unbalanced. The helper returns TRUE when the buffer ends inside an unfinished <… tag, or when a stack-based scan of the tags finds non-void, non-self-closed elements still open. Whatever remains is flushed at end of stream, where the full message is balanced. Two guards limit the hold. A new constant MAX_HTML_BUFFER_SIZE (102400 bytes) forces a flush if a tag never closes, so malformed output cannot grow the buffer without bound. The hold is also skipped while a streaming guardrail is registered ($streamingGuardrailStates non-empty), because guardrails do their own start/stop buffering and holding the buffer across their markers would change what they evaluate. The commit adds a unit test, StreamedHtmlIntegrityTest, that re-chunks HTML at several sizes and checks that it round-trips unchanged.

Contribution

  • Opened: June 22, 2026

item.title: #3582968: Tool Explorer execute form: masked exception on access denial, duplicate messages, no validation pass
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3582968 · 1 contributor · 24 comments

Summary

The Tool Explorer's execute form now reports each outcome once and correctly. Previously, a denied execution showed the real denial plus a confusing "Error executing tool: The action result cannot be retrieved…" message, and every failed run showed both a green status and a red error message. Invalid input is now caught during form validation and shown as inline field errors rather than as a generic failure after submit. The tool label and description header is also built from render elements instead of concatenated markup.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ExecuteToolPluginForm now owns result reporting. submitConfigurationForm() checks the declared permission, extracts the values, checks $this->plugin->access(NULL, TRUE) (including the access result's reason when available), then executes and reports: addStatus() for success, addError() ("Tool execution failed: …") for failure. Denials go through a new reportAccessDenied(), which sets a failure result with FailureCategory::Access via setFailureResult() when the tool has no result yet, and adds an error message. Input extraction moved into a shared extractInputValues() used by both validation and submit.

The new validateConfigurationForm() returns early if the declared permission is not allowed. Otherwise it extracts the inputs and runs validateInputValue() for each input. Violations are joined into one message and set with $form_state->setError() on $form[$name]['value'] if present, else on the wrapper element (for Entity and List adapters). A ContextException from getExecutableValue() is skipped, since an empty required input already fails #required validation.

In ToolExecuteForm (tool_explorer), submitForm() no longer reads getResult() and only delegates to the plugin form. A new validateForm() delegates the same way, and a getPluginForm() helper removes the duplicated class resolution. The header uses a container with html_tag h2 and p elements. Tests were added (ToolExecuteFormTest, ExecuteToolPluginFormTest) plus two test tools, MultiConstraintTool and RegexConstrainedTool.

item.title: #3589006: Default skills output_directory to .claude/skills when Claude Code is detected
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3589006 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Claude Code only loads project skills from .claude/skills/, but ai_best_practices synced skills into .agents/skills/ by default, so Claude Code users got no skills unless they changed the setting by hand. Now, when ai_best_practices.yaml is first created, the plugin picks .claude/skills if it detects Claude Code. Otherwise it keeps .agents/skills. Existing projects keep whatever their yaml already says. Agents that read only .agents/skills will not see the skills in a project that picked .claude/skills.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_best_practices.yaml files get skills.output_directory: .claude/skills when Claude Code is detected (CLAUDECODE or CLAUDE_CODE env var, or a .claude/ directory), otherwise .agents/skills.

Technical details

The issue proposed detecting Claude Code at sync time, whenever skills.output_directory is unset. That could never fire, because ai_best_practices.yaml.dist hardcodes output_directory: .agents/skills and gets copied into every project. The commit instead runs detection once, at file creation. ComposerProjectSynchronizer now reads the .dist template, calls the new SkillsConfig::detectDefaultOutputDirectory($projectRoot), and rewrites the first output_directory: line through a regex in withOutputDirectory(). The Composer message then reports the chosen value, for example "skills output: .claude/skills". The commit message does not give a reason for this change. The SkillsConfig docblock says it keeps the directory from changing depending on who runs Composer later.

Detection is in SkillsConfig::isClaudeCodeProject(). It returns true if the CLAUDECODE or CLAUDE_CODE environment variable is set, or if $projectRoot/.claude is a directory. The directory check covers container wrappers that don't forward the variable (older DDEV, Lando, docker compose exec).

The skills-sync command description and help text and the script usage output no longer hardcode OUTPUT_SKILLS_DIR. They now say skills.output_directory. The .dist comment, the README files and the agent setup docs are updated to match. ComposerProjectSynchronizerTest gains cases for each env var, a .claude/ directory, neither, and an existing config. I did not check the open items in the issue body about SkillsScanner::scanAllSkills() and hand-written skills already in .claude/skills/. The diff does not touch the scanner.

Upgrade

Existing projects are not changed. To get the new behavior, set the value in ai_best_practices.yaml yourself, or delete the file so it is regenerated on the next Composer install or update:

skills:
  output_directory: .claude/skills

Contribution

Timeline

item.title: #3583083: Entity input violation tells an in-process invoker that it cannot pass entities
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583083 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

When a non-entity value (such as a node ID) was set on an entity input, Tool told every invoker without the entity handle capability that it "cannot pass entities". That was false for in-process invokers like ECA, which hand real entity objects to tools. The validation message now states only the reason, "This input must be an entity.", for every invoker. drush tool:run still gives its own advice to use a tool that takes an entity type and ID.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR violation code, set on the violation for a non-entity value on an entity input.

Technical details

The first fix attempt, from #3583046, keyed the hint on InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles. That capability only says whether an invoker uses handle strings. It does not say whether the invoker can carry a PHP object. The fix drops the invoker check from TypedInputsTrait. Validation cannot know what an invoker can supply, because any module may turn what an invoker sent into an entity through an input transform. The violation is now always This input must be an entity. and carries the new code TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR.

An invoker that knows its own boundary can match on that code and add its own advice instead of matching on the message. ToolRunCommand does this. When a failed run, not an access denial, has a violation with that code, it appends drush tool:run cannot pass entities; use a tool that takes an entity type and ID instead. The check covers list items and map properties too. Tests cover the message and code with no invoker, a capability-less invoker and a handles invoker, and check that the code survives the path rebuild for list items. They also check that Drush adds the advice only for entity violations.

item.title: #3583108: Check view label access before including an entity label in handle hints and Drush output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583108 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Tool no longer shows an entity's label to an account that is not allowed to see it. Before, the label: line of a handle hint and the label in drush tool:run output could reveal, for example, the title of another author's unpublished node to a user with only "access content". Now the label is shown only when core's view label check passes, and is otherwise omitted (NULL).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Information disclosure: labels (such as the title of an unpublished node) of entities the account cannot view were shown in handle hints and Drush tool:run output.
  • API change: EntityHandleTransformer::getAccessibleLabel() gains an optional ?AccountInterface $account parameter (current user by default) and now requires view label access on the entity.

Technical details

EntityHandleTransformer::getAccessibleLabel() now first requires $entity->access('view label', $account). Where the entity type has a label field, it also still requires field view access on it. Entity types without a label field, such as user, get only the entity check. The new optional $account defaults to the current user. Handle hints are built while the tool runner has switched to the run-as account, so they omit it.

Drush prints after the runner has switched back from the --uid account, so a plain check there would use the wrong user. The formatOutputValue() and referenceEntities() methods moved from ToolOutputTrait into ToolRunCommand and now take the run-as account. ToolRunCommand gets EntityHandleTransformer (tool.entity_handle_transformer) injected through its constructor. Content entities go through getAccessibleLabel($value, $account). Config entities, which have no field access, use a bare view label check, which the code comment says matches the JSON:API split. Kernel tests cover both paths, with a new tool_test_entity_field_access() hook in the tool_test module to deny title field access.

Upgrade

Custom code that calls getAccessibleLabel() outside a tool run, where the current user is not the account of interest, should pass the account explicitly:

$label = $transformer->getAccessibleLabel($entity, $account);

Code that subclasses or constructs ToolRunCommand directly must supply the new EntityHandleTransformer constructor argument. The class is final and autowired, so this mainly affects manual instantiation.

Contribution

item.title: #3583005: Advertise truthful formats for unmarked datetimes and timestamps
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583005 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

Tool input schemas now describe what Drupal actually accepts. Timestamp inputs advertise integer seconds as well as RFC 3339 strings, so strict clients such as the MCP bridge, which validates arguments against the schema, no longer reject a bare integer. Datetime inputs with no date-only or date-time marker advertise both a full date-time and a bare date, instead of core's date-only date. Output schemas are not changed. If you have clients or tests that depend on the old advertised schema, expect the output of schema normalization to differ.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Advertised input JSON schema changes: core-path timestamp inputs become type: ["string","integer"] (plus null if optional); unmarked datetime_iso8601 inputs advertise anyOf of date-time and date formats.

Technical details

The change is in InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer (src/Normalizer/InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer.php). The issue text proposed advertising plain format: "date-time" for unmarked datetimes. The committed code differs: for an unmarked datetime_iso8601 input, it removes format and emits anyOf: [{format: date-time}, {format: date}], with the description note "An RFC 3339 date-time, or a date alone as YYYY-MM-DD." The comments in the code give the reason: the input coercion subscriber re-emits a full datetime in canonical form but leaves a bare Y-m-d date untouched, and naming only date-time would make a strict invoker reject the bare date. Marked definitions are unchanged: DateOnly gives date, DateTime gives date-time.

For timestamp on the core (11.1+) path, an input schema of type: string is widened to ["string", "integer"]. The note becomes "An RFC 3339 date-time or a Unix timestamp in seconds." This is skipped for OutputDefinitionInterface objects, because the output transform sends the string core describes. The legacy path already used integer and keeps its Unix-seconds note. The optional-input handling now also appends null to an array-valued type, so a union gains the null branch the same way a single string type does. Unmarked datetime outputs are deliberately left alone, since the output transform only rewrites to RFC 3339 under the DateTime marker. The commit also updates the schema matrix and acceptance tests.

item.title: #3583043: Output definitions cannot say "always present, may be null"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583043 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Output definitions can now say a value is always sent but may be null, such as a photo's EXIF date or a timestamp that has not happened yet. Before, one required flag meant both "key must be present" and "never null", so such outputs were published as optional and possibly missing. This also changes existing behavior: an optional output that holds NULL is now left out of the result, and its published schema no longer advertises null. The change landed before rc1 because it alters the published schema of every optional output.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Custom classes implementing OutputDefinitionInterface must implement isNullable() and setNullable(). Optional outputs set to NULL are now omitted from the result, and their schema no longer includes null.
  • New API: nullable constructor parameter and isNullable() / setNullable() on output definitions (OutputDefinitionInterface, NullableOutputTrait), default FALSE.

Technical details

required now means key presence only. A new nullable flag, default FALSE, means null is a value the output carries. This is provided by NullableOutputTrait (isNullable() / setNullable()), added to OutputDefinitionInterface and to the OutputDefinition, ListOutputDefinition, MapOutputDefinition and EntityOutputDefinition constructors as a trailing bool $nullable = FALSE argument.

The four combinations behave as follows:

  • required: TRUE, nullable: FALSE: the key is always present and never null.
  • required: TRUE, nullable: TRUE: the key is always present, may be null, and is listed in the parent's required with [T, "null"] as its type.
  • required: FALSE, nullable: FALSE: an output holding NULL is left out of the result.
  • required: FALSE, nullable: TRUE: the output may be missing or null, and its type is [T, "null"].

InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer reads isNullable() for outputs and strips the null branch (removeNullBranch()) from non-nullable outputs. Inputs keep the old rule, where an optional input is nullable. EffectiveDataDefinition does not mark a nullable output required, so core's NotNull is not added.

Runtime handling is in several places. setOutputValue() and ToolBase drop an optional non-nullable output set to NULL. validateOutputs() uses array_key_exists() to tell "set to NULL" from "never set", so a required nullable output set to NULL passes. The same rule applies inside maps through RecursiveToolValueTransformSubscriber: a null in an optional, non-nullable property is removed. A null list item is not removed, because that would shift the positions after it. It fails validation unless the item definition is nullable. ListOutputDefinition::createFrom() carries the flag on the list itself and sets it FALSE on the item.

TypedMethodDescriber now maps nullable method-tool return types and members to required plus nullable. omit_when_null maps to optional and non-nullable. memberIsRequired() and its @todo were replaced by memberAllowsNull(). Input-side nullable is left to a follow-up issue.

Upgrade

For an output that is always sent and may hold null, declare both flags:

new OutputDefinition('timestamp', 'Date', 'When the photo was taken.', required: TRUE, nullable: TRUE);

Optional outputs that relied on sending an explicit null now need nullable: TRUE. Without it, a NULL value is dropped from the result and the schema no longer lists null.

item.description:

Summary

OAuth2 tokens now record the client identifier (the same value the server uses in requests and in the access token aud claim) in a new client_id field. Before, a token only pointed to a saved consumer entity. This is groundwork for allowing clients that are not saved consumer entities (#3630879). Existing tokens are filled in by a database update, so run updates after deploying. The old client reference is kept.

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: simple_oauth_update_8609() installs a new indexed client_id string field on oauth2_token and backfills it from each token's referenced consumer.
  • New API: New client_id base field on the oauth2_token entity type, holding the OAuth2 client identifier the token was issued to.

Oauth2Token::baseFieldDefinitions() adds a non-translatable client_id string field (max length 255) and lists it in field_indexes. TokenEntityNormalizer sets it from $client->getIdentifier(). RefreshTokenEntityNormalizer sets it from $token_entity->getAccessToken()->getClient()->getIdentifier(). The client entity reference is still written by TokenEntityNormalizer.

simple_oauth_update_8609() installs the field storage definition. It then copies client_id from consumer_field_data (default language rows only) into oauth2_token, matching on the token's client column. Tokens with no consumer reference stay NULL.

Kernel tests cover token creation across the authorization code flow and the update path. The unit test for the collector was adjusted for the OR group.

Run database updates (drush updb) to apply simple_oauth_update_8609(), which adds the client_id field to oauth2_token and backfills existing tokens from their consumers.

The ai_best_practices project has a new skill, drupal-ckeditor5-plugins, for AI coding agents that customize CKEditor 5 in Drupal. It targets three recurring agent mistakes: reading the latest CKEditor docs instead of the version bundled in the site's core, shipping raw ES modules where Drupal 10.3 to 11 needs a webpack DLL bundle, and mixing the DLL method with the new-builds (UMD) method used from Drupal 12 and CKEditor 5 v48. item.title: #3583065: Report item and property positions in the violation path, not the message
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583065 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Tool module, a validation failure on a list item or map property now reports where it happened in the violation's property path (code, codes.0, rows.0.sku). Before, the position was embedded in the message text, e.g. (item 0) .... Output validation failures now follow the same shape as input failures: the output name is on the path and the message states only the reason. The plain-text failure message still shows the path in front of each reason, so Drush-style text consumers still see where the failure is. Code that parsed (item N) or (property x) out of messages, or that matched the old output messages, needs updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Violation property paths for list items and map properties now carry the position (code, codes.0, rows.0.sku); the (item N) and (property x) message prefixes are gone. Output violations carry the output name on the path with generic messages, and getViolations() is now populated on output failures.

Technical details

ValueViolationsTrait::addItemViolations() no longer takes a $kind argument and no longer wraps the message. It rebuilds each violation with static::joinPath($position, $violation->getPropertyPath()), and now also passes the constraint through to the new violation. validateInputValues() now uses it for the input name too, replacing its own rebuild loop. TypedOutputsTrait::validateOutputs() uses it to put the output name on the path. getItemDefinitionForViolations() is removed, since messages no longer need the item's label, and callers use $definition->getItemDefinition().

Messages that named the value by label became generic and name-free, because the name is now on the path: This output is required but was not provided., This property is required., This output must be an entity., This output is invalid: @type.. The required-output violation now carries the output name as its path instead of an empty string.

ToolBase now builds the Runtime failure from ToolMessages::violationList($violations) and passes $violations to ExecutableResult::failure(). ToolResultInterface::getViolations() therefore covers output failures as well as input failures. Callers can use getFailureCategory() to tell an input they can correct from an output the tool got wrong. The ToolResultInterface docblock documents the path format: the name is the segment before the first dot, and a map property reads product.sku, a list item codes.0, both rows.0.sku.

Upgrade

Read the position from the violation path instead of the message. Messages like (item 0) This value should be of the correct primitive type. are now path codes.0 with the message This value should be of the correct primitive type.

foreach ($result->getViolations() as $violation) {
  $path = $violation->getPropertyPath(); // e.g. "rows.0.sku"; first segment is the input or output name.
}

item.title: #3583086: Let `destructive` be undeclared, so write tools aren't reported as non-destructive
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI

Summary

The Tool module can now tell a tool that never declared destructive apart from one that said it is not destructive. An undeclared Write or Trigger tool is now treated as destructive, and an undeclared Read tool is not. Before, every write tool that left the flag out looked non-destructive, so the MCP bridge told clients it only added data. That is the opposite of MCP's own default. Authors of write tools that only add data should now set destructive: FALSE explicitly.

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: destructive on #[Tool], #[ToolMethod] and ToolDefinition::setDestructive() is now ?bool defaulting to NULL (undeclared); ToolDefinition::isDestructive() answers from the operation when undeclared.

destructive on the #[Tool] and #[ToolMethod] attributes and the ToolDefinition::$destructive property changed from bool defaulting to FALSE to ?bool defaulting to NULL. ToolDefinition::setDestructive() accepts ?bool. ToolDefinition::isDestructive() now returns $this->destructive ?? $this->getOperation()->isModifying(). ToolOperation::isModifying() is TRUE for Write and Trigger and FALSE for Explain, Read and Transform. An explicit TRUE or FALSE always wins over the operation. #[ToolMethod] defaults its operation to Write, so a method that omits destructive is now destructive.

The Drush ToolGenerator prompt now defaults its answer to what an undeclared tool would get for the chosen operation. tool.twig always writes destructive: TRUE or FALSE instead of omitting it when false, so answering no on a Write tool is an explicit declaration. The issue body says the MCP bridge (mcp_server_tool_bridge) sends this as destructiveHint. The commit does not touch that bridge, which gets the new value through isDestructive(). The issue was meant to land before the RC1 freeze (#3582976).

Write or Trigger tools that only add data and relied on the old default must now say so:

#[ToolMethod(id: 'tool_test.notebook.export', operation: ToolOperation::Write, permission: 'access content', destructive: FALSE)]

Code that passes destructive: FALSE or TRUE is unchanged. Code that reads isDestructive() still gets a bool.

item.title: #3583091: Name the input when an entity handle fails, so getViolations() covers handle failures
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583091 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When a tool call is given a malformed, missing or wrong-type entity handle, the failed result now says which input was at fault. Before, getViolations() was empty for these failures and the message was only a generic "Invalid input" text. A caller, such as an AI agent, can now see every bad input in one response and fix them together.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

HandleExceptionInterface is a bare marker with no input context, so ToolRunner could only produce Invalid input: @message with no violations. The issue weighed two options: a per-input catch in the runner, or an InputAwareExceptionInterface with getInputNames(). The merged code takes the per-input catch. It adds no new interface.

In ToolRunner, the loop that calls $tool->setInputValue() now catches HandleExceptionInterface for each input. It records a ConstraintViolation whose property path is the input name, built by the new private handleViolation(). A HandleNotFoundException gets an extra sentence saying a handle resolves only for the account that created it, until it expires. A refiner that throws is attributed to the input whose set triggered it.

The loop also catches InputException per input. Its named violations join the same list. A bare-reason exception keeps its own message as the whole result unless another input has already failed. The runner collects every input that cannot be stored before refusing the call. It then runs validateInputs() on the inputs that were stored and adds those violations, skipping the inputs that failed to store, so a bad value shows up beside a bad handle. The combined list is set with setFailureResult() using FailureCategory::Input. The private inputNamed() reads the first segment of a violation path to do that filtering. The outer HandleExceptionInterface catch remains only for handle exceptions thrown after the input loop, such as an output transform, which have no input to name.

Summary

In AI Context, agents can no longer subscribe to Languages. A language tag on an item no longer ranks it higher for an agent. Items are still dropped when the request language doesn't match, and they are still included in Relevant and Broad when it does. In Minimal mode, items tagged only with a language are no longer injected unless they use Always include. Existing language subscriptions stay in agent config but are ignored. Sites without Dynamic Entity Reference now list Specific Entities as Unavailable on the scope overview, where it used to be missing. Rebuild caches after updating. item.title: #3586388: Align scope scoring, language service, and contextual selection behavior
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586388 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

Scope ordering, subscription scoring and language handling in AI Context now follow one rule. A scope plugin's weight sets both its position in the UI and its influence on scoring, and higher values come first. Entity Bundle and Site Section scoped items are now excluded when no entity or request is available, instead of staying eligible. Content language is now detected the same way for selection, the language scope, and the list and load-by-id function calls. This includes AJAX calls that carry the language only in the Referer header.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Scope plugin weight now means higher = displayed first and scored more strongly (previously lower = first). The AiContextScope attribute default weight changed from 0 to 1, and AiContextScopeBase::getWeight() falls back to 1.
  • New API: New ai_context.detected_language cache context, used by selection cache metadata.

Technical details

Built-in weights are now Global 100, Use Case 70, Entity Type (shown as Entity Bundle) 60, Site Section 50, Tag 40, Language 30 and Specific Entities (entity_item) 10. Scores use the weight directly through a max(1, weight) clamp in AiContextScopeResolver, replacing abs(weight) + 1. Scoring skips scopes where supportsSubscriptions() is FALSE. For plugin IDs with no plugin instance it also skips global, entity_item and target_entity. AiContextScopeManager sorts by weight descending with plugin ID as the tiebreaker. It no longer lists ai_context provider plugins before other modules, so custom plugins can fall between built-ins.

The new Drupal\ai_context\Service\AiContextLanguageService (ai_context.language_service, marked @internal) provides detect(), translateItem() and translateItems(). It replaces AiContextLanguageDetectorTrait, which is deleted, and the private translateItems() copies in AiContextSelector and LoadAiContextItemById. AiContextSelector, AiContextScopeLanguage, ListAiContextItems and LoadAiContextItemById all use it. The AiContextSelector constructor now takes the language service in place of LanguageManagerInterface. AiContextItemRevisionOverviewForm drops its unused languageManager argument. A new AiContextDetectedLanguageCacheContext returns detect() as its value and itself depends on languages:language_content and url.path. AiContextSelector now uses it in place of languages:language_content.

AiContextScopeEntityType gains matchesCurrentContext(): no item values gives NULL (neutral), no current value gives FALSE, otherwise a match test. AiContextScopeSiteSection returns FALSE instead of NULL when there is no current request. ListAiContextItems seeds the current entity from entity_type and entity_id through AiContextCurrentEntityResolver::setCurrentEntity() before filterByCurrentContext(), and clears it in a finally block.

Custom scope plugins that declared a weight for the old "lower is first" ordering need new values. For example, the built-in plugins changed like this:

weight: 100,   // was -100
// AiContextScopeUseCase
weight: 70,    // was -10
// AiContextScopeLanguage
weight: 30,    // was 0

Pick a value between the built-in weights (for example 65, between Use Case and Entity Bundle) to place a custom scope. Code that calls ListAiContextItems for bundle-scoped content must pass entity_type and entity_id, because bundle-scoped items are now rejected when no entity can be resolved.
